steps.title: Report
steps.actor: Anyone: user, support, team. An AI helps fill it in, without guessing what is missing
out: Fixed-format form: steps, expected, observed, version or date, optional capture, perceived severity

steps.title: Code checks
out: Complete form, existing version or date, readable capture if present

steps.title: Auditor
steps.actor: AI: a single auditor, who holds the discussion with the human
in: Functional guidelines, vocabulary, personas. Selected by script, index first
Need entries and user flows whose scope overlaps the report's, with their log
ADRs whose scope overlaps the report's
out: Proposed qualification, with citation: gap on criterion or step X, or uncovered behavior, or conforms to decision Y (log or ADR), or technical defect with no visible criterion, or duplicate of T-n
Proposed severity: blocking, major or minor
Proposed scope, drawn from the project vocabulary. To validate at the gate

steps.title: Code checks
out: The cited criterion, step, decision or ticket exists, scope from the vocabulary, a qualification and a severity present

steps.title: Judge
steps.actor: AI, three fixed questions, citation required

questions.q: Does the cited criterion, step or decision really concern the reported behavior?
Is the cited duplicate really one?
Does the report's expectation contradict an option discarded in a log?

out: Yes or no: does the cited criterion, step or decision really concern the reported behavior? is a cited duplicate really one? does the report's expectation contradict an option discarded in a log?

steps.title: Gate · Qualification
steps.actor: Human F, or human T for a technical defect. Mandatory unless the qualification is "gap" and the judge and checks are green
in: Code checks and judge, all green
out: Or other qualification: back to the audit, with the reason
Or incomplete report: back to the person reporting

steps.title: Direction
in: Qualification validated, or "gap" without a gate
out: Gap: Recette workflow to launch. Input ready: the reference (the cited criteria or user flow), the report's version, the suggested persona if any. The Recette alone creates the correction ticket if it fails
Uncovered behavior: Need workflow to launch. Input ready: the report as a request, with its proposed scope
Technical defect: Plan workflow to launch, entry 2. Input ready: the report as a technical need, with its proposed scope
Conforms: reasoned answer to the person, citing the log or the ADR, then closure
Duplicate: link to the existing ticket or report, then closure
Recette without gap: the defect is not reproduced, a request for details goes to the person, then closure after the delay set by the project

contract: A defect noticed outside a Recette, by a user, support or the team.
A validated qualification, then depending on the case: a reproduction Recette, an entry to reframe, a technical need, or a reasoned closure.
The person reporting, then human F to decide, or human T for a technical defect. No gate if the qualification is "gap" and the judge and checks are green: the Recette that follows has its own.
notes: It fixes nothing and creates no ticket. It qualifies, names the next workflow and prepares its input. The human launches that workflow by hand.
A single producer of correction tickets
The Recette. Report never creates them itself: every correction ticket thus has a Recette record behind it.
Same qualification vocabulary as the Recette
Gap (bug), uncovered behavior or wrong expectation (Need), technical defect (Plan). It is defined in one place.
The judge and the code checks replace it. The gate is mandatory, except for a "gap" that the Recette then verifies.
The proposed severity orders the correction tickets. A blocking severity can justify using the Express workflow.
doc.lede: A person notices abnormal behavior outside a Recette. The workflow qualifies it, then sends it to the right place. It never creates a correction ticket: only the Recette does.
